title: Typed output sentinel: compatibility & constrained-decoding benchmark
creator: Samira Khan
description: Objective: Build a reproducible benchmark and test harness to validate schema adherence across streaming, function/tool-calling, and constrained-decoding modes. This ticket covers test generation, CI integration, metrics, and a playbook for classifying failures. The goal is to detect regressions introduced by kernel changes, KV cache tweaks, or streaming reassembly logic. Scope excludes end-to-end customer prompts — we will use synthetic and anonymized seed prompts and property-based inputs.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic test harness that runs nightly and on PRs for runtime changes
Covering matrix: streaming vs non-streaming, toolcall interleaving vs no-tools, model family variants (Llama- and MPT-like), and constrained-decoder toggles
Pass/fail metrics: schema-pass-rate >= 99% on baseline models; categorized failure buckets for partial-JSON, extra-fields, missing-required-fields, and malformed-types
CI dashboard with historical trends and alerting when drop > 2 percentage points vs baseline
Runbook describing rollback and temporary decoder-backoff policy to apply in flight
test_plan: Harness design: 1) Corpus: 1k templated prompts + 500 fuzzed permutations that exercise edge cases (escaped characters, truncated streams, function-call offsets). 2) Executors: local unit runner, staging CI workers with streaming simulation, and a nightly cluster job on dedicated test GPUs. 3) Validators: JSON Schema v4-based strict validator plus a leniency mode that reports partial-recoverable errors. 4) Metrics: per-example verdict, wall-time, token count, and latency distribution. 5) Fault injections: simulate dropped chunks, reordering, and mixed toolcall tokens to verify reassembly logic. 6) Backstop: automatic creation of a GitHub issue when a new failure pattern emerges and a tagged sample request to reproduce locally.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created and scoped; initial corpus templates drafted; assigned Miguel for infra work.
2026-03-11: Scoped streaming injection harness; drafted schema set and validator rules; opened spike PR for local runner: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2148

2026-03-12: Design review with PM and QA; agreed to add toolcall-interleaving scenarios and an early-warning metric for partial-JSON regressions. Miguel started provisioning staging workers. Blocking: need test GPU quota in test org (request submitted to infra).
risks_mitigation: Risk: Flaky test results due to upstream model nondeterminism. Mitigation: use deterministic seeds where possible, record model version pins in artifacts, run per-commit against a pinned baseline, and treat ephemeral failures as flaky with threshold-based retries before alerting. Risk: test infra saturates CI. Mitigation: schedule heavy runs to nightly cluster jobs and keep PR gate tests fast (~30s smoke).
notes: We should coordinate with Runtime SRE for kernel rollout windows; consider tagging failing examples with hardware profile to identify kernel/hw-specific regressions. Also propose an internal label 'sot-test-failure' for triaging. Consider future expansion to include token-gating/backpressure scenarios and Dedicated capacity invariants.
